  "text": "By morning, the harbor had fallen three feet. Mud shone between the pilings, threaded with things the tide had kept for years: a spoon, a child’s boot, the white ribs of a skiff. Mara’s father went down with the harbor master to check the gate. The woman stayed beside the lantern.

Its flame was yellow again. She watched it anyway.

Mara set the bell on the sill. The scratched name was ELIAS, the same name the woman had whispered when the distant light appeared. Mara wanted to ask whether she had recognized his signal in the pipe, but the woman had already heard her father’s footsteps on the stairs.

“The wheel won’t turn,” he said. “We can’t open it.”

“Good,” the woman answered. She picked up the bell. For the first time, Mara noticed a second line of marks beneath the name: seven little strokes, and an eighth cut deeper than the rest.

Outside, a shout rose from the mud. The harbor master had found a length of rope caught beneath the gate. Mara’s father hauled it free, hand over hand. At the end was a wooden float, painted blue. Its iron hook had been bent almost straight.

The woman took it from him. “He used to mark the channel with these,” she said.

Mara looked past her to the glass. In daylight it reflected only the room and the three of them standing close together. Below it, water still seeped through the grate. The woman hung the float on a nail by the door, where anyone coming down the stairs would see it."
